auth_bypass.description: Authentication or token verification is bypassed or disabled.

command_injection.description: Untrusted or unsafe command execution reaches shell/process sinks.

cors.description: CORS policy is overly permissive or credential unsafe.

deserialization.description: Untrusted data reaches unsafe deserialization APIs.

path_traversal.description: Untrusted path segments reach filesystem sinks.

precision_guard.description: Clean patterns that should stay free of noisy security findings.

prompt_injection.description: Hidden, disguised or encoded instructions aimed at AI tools, and text that only resembles them.

sensitive_logging.description: Credential-source data reaches output, with redaction and response-data controls.

sql_injection.description: Untrusted data reaches SQL construction or execution.

ssrf.description: Untrusted data controls outbound request destinations.

tls_verification.description: TLS peer verification settings and provider identity controls.

weak_hash.description: MD5/SHA1 warnings, explicit nonsecurity use and strong-hash lookalikes.

weak_random.description: Security-sensitive random values and the identity of their source.

xss.description: Untrusted data reaches HTML or script rendering sinks.

cases.description: Request-supplied SQL passed through a helper remains injection even when execute() binds a separate ID value.
Statically built SQL using constant .format() arguments should not be reported as SQL injection.
A request parameter interpolated into the URL host of a route handler should be detected as SSRF.
A helper whose URL host comes only from its own parameter (no route, request, CLI, MCP-tool or stdin source) is not reported as SSRF.
Fixed-host URL interpolation should not be reported as SSRF when only the path segment is tainted.
subprocess imported with an alias should still be detected when shell=True is used.
yaml.load with positional yaml.SafeLoader should not be reported as unsafe deserialization.
User-controlled path segments joined into a filesystem path should be reported as path traversal.
Path input sanitized with os.path.basename before opening a fixed directory should stay quiet.
Tainted HTML interpolated into Markup should be reported as XSS.
Escaped content wrapped with Markup should not be reported as XSS.
User-controlled redirect targets should be reported as open redirect.
A leading-slash check still accepts protocol-relative external redirect targets.
A redirect restricted to explicit local destinations should stay quiet.
JWT decode with signature verification disabled should be reported.
Wildcard CORS configuration should be reported.
An ordinary Requests client explicitly disables certificate verification.
The paired Requests client explicitly keeps certificate verification enabled.
A native client context is made non-verifying through an alias after its secure-looking constructor.
A native PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT context preserves certificate and hostname verification.
A local inert helper stores a similarly named option and performs no TLS operation.
Import-time code replaces the inert-looking helper with BrowserConfig, so the later disabling option retains a finding.
A replaced CERT_REQUIRED value cannot prove certificate checking is enabled.
A native legacy client context has both chain and hostname verification explicitly enabled.
Password bytes enter native hashlib.md5; weak algorithm remains a finding.
Explicit usedforsecurity=False marks a nonsecurity content fingerprint under the documented opt-out policy.
The aliased hashlib.new factory explicitly chooses SHA1 over an API token.
The native factory uses the explicit nonsecurity opt-out.
SHA256 is neither MD5 nor SHA1. This control makes no claim that unsalted SHA256 is an adequate password storage scheme.
A local method named md5 actually uses SHA256 and is not a native weak-hash API.
A cache_key name does not prove nonsecurity use; the value is a credential and security use is explicitly true.
Native random.getrandbits controls a session cookie value.
Native secrets.token_urlsafe supplies cookie entropy.
SystemRandom uses OS entropy rather than random.Random PRNG state.
Randomness changes retry delay, not a credential, cookie or authentication value.
The weak value is overwritten with strong entropy before the only security sink.
One reachable branch replaces strong entropy with random.getrandbits before the cookie sink.
A local random-named method delegates to secrets.token_urlsafe; no native weak-random source exists.
Credential environment data reaches a real logger unchanged.
A password-like variable name holds an explicitly public literal, not credential source data.
The credential binding is overwritten with a literal before output.
The branch where redaction is declined still sends the credential to logging.
The HTTP response status is server data; it is not the password in the request payload.
The response URL retains the credential query parameter sent in the request.
The helper named redact explicitly returns its input unchanged; its name cannot prove redaction.
Mutating the shared container through an alias actually removes the credential before logging.
Rebinding the alias leaves the original credential-bearing container unchanged.
The weak-module alias is explicitly rebound to native SystemRandom before its only credential sink.
The secrets alias is explicitly rebound to native random.Random before its cookie entropy call.
Request bytes are passed directly to the actual pickle.loads provider.
A captured pickle.loads function still deserializes request bytes.
Rebinding the pickle module name to json does not change a previously captured pickle.loads callable.
The module name is rebound to json before loads is looked up, so this call parses data without unpickling.
A source-owned DataParser.loads method returns its input and does not unpickle.
A captured json.loads callable parses JSON and is not a pickle provider.
Request text reaches the builtin eval function directly.
Request text reaches the builtin eval function captured in a variable.
A source-owned function named eval returns text without interpreting it.
Request text reaches the real subprocess.run provider with shell=True.
A captured subprocess.run provider still executes request text with shell=True.
A source-owned DataSink.run method accepts a shell keyword but only returns its input.
Ukrainian and Greek translation files with JSON escapes, zero-width characters passed as whole literals to str.replace, and Japanese text with word-break hints.
A Cyrillic letter inside Latin identifiers (also inside a translation file) and a zero-width character splitting an instruction keyword.
self._session_replacements is only ever a dict, so .get(key) is a lookup and not an HTTP request.
The same attribute can also hold an httpx.Client, so .get(value) can be a request to a request-supplied URL.
The printed values are the key file path and a mask that keeps six leading and four trailing characters.
The raw key is printed next to its masked form.
A helper named redact returns the whole key without dashes; its name is not a proof.
The module name is a value of a constant table; the command-line argument only selects a key.
The table lookup falls back to the raw command-line argument, so any module can be imported.
A Path annotation may still hold a Hub repository id; offline-only and explicit absolute-path controls do not fetch mutable artifacts.
A str parameter may be a Hub repository id, so the download has no pinned revision.
The route rejects every name that does not fully match letters, digits, dash and underscore before joining it into a path.
match without an end anchor accepts a/../../x, so the joined path can leave the directory.
re.search finds one allowed character anywhere; ../x still passes.
FastMCP takes host=0.0.0.0 in its constructor and run() starts a network transport without authentication.
The same constructor host is unused when the server runs on stdio; no socket is opened.
A helper reads the key and builds a client; the printed value is an API result of that client, not the key.
